recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No further core source work is indicated for FHIR-16981 unless a future work group decision reopens broader Address versus Location modeling guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-16981 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core datatype issue asking to clarify the apparent contradiction between the Address note, which said addresses were postal and not physical locations, and Address.type, which distinguishes physical visitable addresses from mailing addresses.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in SVN revision 14323, represented by git commit 12b8d31a181d6993a9a8afab92d08c249a8fbc37, which added a clarifying Address.type comment about addresses that can be visited as well as used for delivery.
additional_context: FHIR-17722 later approved the precise replacement wording for the same contradictory Address note and is already represented on the combined branch by cad4329c7d74e5d795f735415b2115783af7de9a. FHIR-42765 later touched nearby Address datatype guidance and is also already represented. Address is listed in source/fhir.ini's active [types] section, and community searches found no Zulip or Confluence record that conflicts with the Jira/source history.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current source/datatypes/address.xml text says Address is expressed using postal conventions for administrative purposes rather than absolute geographic coordinates, that postal addresses are often used as proxies for physical locations, and that Address.type distinguishes postal, physical, and both.
